deposits.notes: The publisher's public file-list API (https://www.frontiersin.org/api/v4/articles/1508383/supplemental-data) returned HTTP 200 and listed exactly one supplementary file. Downloaded https://public-pages-files-2025.frontiersin.org/articles/1508383/file/Table_1.xlsx/1508383_table_1/2 into memory (HTTP 200; final URL https://public-pages-files-2025.frontiersin.org/articles/1508383/file/table_1.xlsx/1508383_table_1/2). The entire workbook was read with openpyxl: one visible sheet named 一定最新的ssci67, 66 nonempty rows consisting of a title row, a header row, and 64 participant records. All 64 IDs are unique; all five columns are complete. Groups=1 contains IDs 1-32 and Groups=2 contains IDs 33-64, with 32 records in each. The workbook does not provide a verbal arm codebook. Mapping Groups=1 to AIGC and Groups=2 to traditional tools is inferred and verified by reproducing every arm-specific mean and sample SD for Creativity, Concentration, and Relaxation in PDF p. 8, Table 1; assignment and arm definitions are in p. 4, section 3.1. Creativity is the final participant-level CSDS composite, not the individual experts' ratings or dimension/item scores. Concentration and Relaxation are participant-level EEG summary scores; no EEG time series, code, transcripts, design texts, prompts, sketches, or rendered designs are included. The article's p. 1 copyright statement is CC BY and links to https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ (HTTP 200); no separate license was stated for the workbook, so the data-license field is null. An initial legacy static-file URL, https://www.frontiersin.org/files/Articles/1508383/fpsyg-16-1508383-HTML-r1/Table_1.xlsx, returned HTTP 404; the current publisher API supplied the working file URL above. what_we_could_compute: For S1-O1 (Creativity/CSDS composite), compute exact arm-specific participant counts, means, sample SDs, SEs of the means, and the SE/confidence interval of the between-arm mean difference from the 64 complete participant scores. Table 1 already prints rounded means, SDs, and analyzed counts; the public rows permit independent verification and additional precision statistics.

This resolves the supplement-content and additional-statistics question in final.open_items[1]: the supplement supplies participant-level composite scores and two EEG summaries, with no additional creativity dimensions or outcomes. Per-person final scores are available, but means across individual experts or CSDS items cannot be reconstructed.
notes: Availability checked on 2026-10-10. Read the complete 634-line markdown conversion through the final references; the saved 15-page PDF has no appended supplement and no embedded files. Checked the availability statements directly in PDF p. 14 and checked Table 1 using PyMuPDF table extraction. Statements below also retain the article's licensing, consent-to-publication, and Figure 4 individual-score descriptions; quotes are copied from the markdown, including the space at the wrapped supplementary URL. The executable URL is normalized in deposits. No preregistration, analysis-code link, or separate data repository is named in the paper, and both form.data_and_code URL fields are empty. The previous form's network failures did not recur: the publisher supplement is now confirmed public. One publisher deposit is counted; unrelated or unlinked search results are not counted as deposits. No login, account creation, access request, or challenge bypass was used, and data were inspected only in memory. No participant designs or idea texts were found, so text/design diversity or homogenization cannot be computed from this workbook. The individual randomization-sequence method (final.open_items[0]) and rater aggregation/blinding protocol (final.open_items[2]) remain unresolved. The statement inviting further inquiries is not treated as an explicit promise of data on request.
